summary: The EU's values and transparency commissioner Vera Jourova said X (formerly Twitter) had the largest ratio of mis/disinformation posts among platforms in a pilot test of new structural indicators under the EU Code of Practice on Disinformation. X left the Code in May but is legally bound by the Digital Services Act, which carries penalties up to 6% of global annual turnover. The article also covers X's rebuttal, Musk's policy changes, X's falling ad revenue, and a NewsGuard report on surging propaganda after state-media labels were removed.
one_line: The EU says X (formerly Twitter) has the worst ratio of disinformation to other posts among major platforms, raising DSA enforcement risk.
key_facts: Vera Jourova, the EU commissioner for values and transparency, said X had the largest ratio of mis/disinformation posts among platforms assessed in a pilot phase.
The pilot was run by Code of Practice signatories in three Member States and evaluated the methodology on two structural indicators.
Structural indicators include how easy disinformation is to find, how much engagement it receives, and indicators about sources.
X exited the EU's Code of Practice on Disinformation in May 2023, shortly after EU lawmakers warned that Musk-era policy shifts were boosting Kremlin propaganda.

X's global government affairs account replied that more than 700 unique Community Notes appeared on posts related to the Ukraine conflict, and its 'Notes on Media' feature put notes on over 1,200 additional posts.
In April 2023, X/Twitter was named one of 19 platforms facing the strictest level of regulation under the EU's DSA (very large online platforms, or VLOPs).
A Commission spokesperson said the Code is voluntary but DSA compliance is not, and the DSA is legally binding on X/Twitter.
The TrustLab study covered Code signatories at the time the exercise launched, which included X/Twitter, before the DSA applied to VLOPs.
DSA penalties can scale up to 6% of global annual turnover.
X's ad revenue has cratered since Musk's takeover amid an advertiser exodus, which would shrink any future DSA penalties.
Musk recently suggested charging all users a small fee; Twitter Blue, now called X Premium, has not plugged the ad revenue gap.
A NewsGuard report found Musk's removal of state-affiliated media labels led to a surge in propaganda on X, with Russia's RT seeing the biggest gains.
X replied to the press request with an automated email reading 'Busy now, please check back later.'
